questions.prompt: In the stem, which tissue carries water upward from the roots?
questions.explanation: Xylem tubes in the stem carry water and minerals upward from the roots to the leaves.
questions.misconception: Some learners think water flows down, but water always travels upward from the root to the leaves where it is used to make food.

questions.prompt: Which tissue in the stem carries the food (sugar) made in the leaves down to the rest of the plant?
questions.explanation: Phloem tubes carry the food that leaves make down to the rest of the plant, where it is used or stored.
questions.misconception: Learners often think the same tubes carry both, or that food moves upward. Food made in leaves travels downward in separate phloem tubes.

questions.prompt: What is one important job of the stem?
options: To support the leaves and flowers up high
To absorb water from the air
questions.explanation: The stem holds the leaves and flowers up high so they catch sunlight and can be reached, and it connects the roots and leaves.
questions.misconception: Some learners think the stem itself makes food, but it does not - it carries and supports; the leaves make the food.

questions.prompt: Where do leaves and flowers attach to a stem?
options: At the nodes along the stem
Only at the very top tip
They never attach to the stem
questions.explanation: Leaves, branches, and flowers attach at points along the stem called nodes.
questions.misconception: Some think parts grow only at the very ends of the stem, but they attach at the nodes along its length.
